title: Modular Terraform EKS controlplane orchestrator with canary healthplay for Private VPC
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable, auditable Terraform module and small orchestration layer to provision Redwood Private EKS control planes inside customer VPCs. The module must be idempotent, support safe rolling upgrades (canary + staged rollouts), expose health checks and observability hooks, and include preflight validations plus a synthetic smoke test runner to reduce upgrade regressions for Private deployments.

Scope:
- Terraform module(s) that create control-plane components (EKS cluster control plane config, control-plane IAM roles, service account mappings, cross-account KMS integration, security groups, vpc endpoints, and necessary SSM/Secrets Manager hooks).
- Preflight validation resources (Terraform validations + init-time scripts) that verify network CIDR, route tables, required endpoints reachable, and KMS+role trust.
- Canary upgrade workflow: a canary control plane (single AZ small control nodes / separate EKS control-plane resource where possible) plus staged rollout and automated health gating, with automatic rollback or marked manual-review on failure.
- Health checks: API server probe, control-plane reconciliation latency, kube-apiserver metrics threshold checks, node readiness trends, and synthetic workload runner that applies a small job exercising scheduling, KV cache warmup, and inference-serving smoke path.
- Observability: emit structured rollout events to Redwood Console ingestion (via CloudWatch Events/ EventBridge -> Console ETL) including tokenized telemetry for latency/cost delta and upgrade status.
- Upgrade safety: cordon/drain strategy, pre- and post-upgrade probes, canary promotion conditions, and a documented runbook.

Out of scope for this ticket: full managed operator that performs upgrades automatically for all customers (this ticket provides primitives and an operator-lite playbook for early customers).

Why now: Recent internal incidents (see related_incidents) showed control-plane upgrades produced transient API errors that affected Dedicated customers. We need a hardened, testable Terraform path for Private deployments to prevent regressions and allow predictable rollouts.

Non-goals: replace upstream EKS managed control-plane behavior; avoid radically changing customer networking models in first pass.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module lives in infra/private/controlplane and follows repo standards (README, examples, variables.tf, outputs.tf)
Applies are idempotent for repeated terraform apply cycles (no drift on repeated apply due to resource ordering) in CI staging environment
Preflight validations detect common misconfigurations (missing VPC endpoints, blocked SGs, wrong KMS key policy) and fail fast with actionable messages
Canary upgrade workflow executed in staging: canary promoted only if 95th percentile API latency and synthetic smoke tests pass for 30 minutes
Rollback or hold occurs automatically if health gates fail, with clear event logged to Console and notification to #infra-ops
End-to-end CI test runs: module provisioning, synthetic smoke test, upgrade canary, and staged promotion (green path) complete reliably in CI pipeline
Documentation and runbook created for SREs and Solutions Engineers with step-by-step canary promotion and emergency rollback
Security review complete and KMS cross-account policy patterns approved
Telemetry and metrics surface in Console dashboard (control-plane rollout timeline + health metrics)
implementation_notes: Terraform version constraint >= 1.5, use required_providers block with pinned AWS provider (>= 5.0)
Module layout: modules/controlplane/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,preflight.tf,canary.tf,examples/} and top-level examples for customer and staging
Use aws_eks_cluster + aws_eks_node_group only where necessary; prefer control-plane config via EKS resource and smaller bootstrapped control-plane components for canary testing
Idempotency: avoid computed timestamps in resource names; prefer stable tags and create lifecycle ignore_changes for non-actionable fields
Preflight: implement null_resource + local-exec validators that run AWS CLI and kubeconfig probes; surface failures as Terraform errors with remediation hints
Health probes: export CloudWatch metrics and create EventBridge rules for threshold alarms that integrate with Console ingestion pipeline

Canary promotion: represent staged rollout using a staged tf workspace approach OR a small orchestration script (Go) that uses terraform apply for each stage and evaluates health gates via CloudWatch + synthetic job results

Synthetic smoke test: small Kubernetes Job created as post-provision hook; Job runs a basic HTTP call to an internal NGINX ingress or small inference container; results collected to S3/CloudWatch logs
KMS: allow optional customer_key_id variable; support both customer-managed and Redwood-managed keys; include recommended key policy for cross-account access and rotation guidance
IAM: least-privilege roles with assume-role boundaries; document which managed policies are required by SRE vs customer admin
Observability hooks: emit structured upgrade events (json) to EventBridge; include fields cluster_id, rollout_id, stage, health_gates_passed, latency_delta
Testing: create Terratest suites (Go) that provision staging cluster variants in sandbox account and run upgrade canary flows; CI job tags should tear down resources on failure
RBAC & secrets: provide example of service account mapping for the synthetic test runner; avoid storing kubeconfig in plaintext in CI logs
Upgrade safety knobs: canary_duration, promote_thresholds, max_concurrent_promotions, pre_drain_delay, post_drain_validation_window
Backward compatibility: design outputs for existing on-prem tooling and ensure module supports import of existing clusters where feasible
comments: 2026-02-25 Avery Chen: Created ticket after week of incident triage. Suggested split between module primitives and operator-lite orchestrator. Assigned to Ravi.
2026-02-27 Ravi Patel: Initial design doc uploaded and linked (see links). Requesting review from security for KMS cross-account pattern.

2026-03-02 Design review notes: PM Sarai suggested adding a simple UI toggle in Console for manual canary promotion (tracked in follow-up PM ticket). Design recommended minimal UI for first iteration.
2026-03-04 PR #1289 opened: initial module scaffolding and example of preflight validators. CI failing on synthetic test timeouts in sandbox account.
2026-03-06 QA: synthetic smoke test flaked in one sandbox run due to insufficient IAM permissions for the test role. Added explicit iam:PassRole and updated example.
2026-03-10 Security review: KMS policy pattern accepted with one change: deny wildcards on kms:Grant*; updated key policy example in module README.
2026-03-12 Ops feedback: prefer EventBridge events to CloudWatch logs for structured rollout data; updated implementation notes and add EventBridge rule mapping.

2026-03-14 Ravi Patel: Addressed CI flakiness by increasing timeout windows and adding exponential backoff to synthetic test runner. Moving to In Progress; next step: Terratest job and final runbook prep.
